heard: Our entire galaxy is sliding toward a central gravitational focal point. For years, astronomers only mapped our cosmic neighbors using light-based positions. In September 2014, researcher R. Brent Tully tracked how these galaxies actually move. Using the Green Bank telescope, his team mapped a structure spanning 400 to 500 million light years. They named it Laniakea, a Hawaiian word meaning immense heaven or open skies. This supercluster contains approximately 100,000 galaxies matching the mass of 100 quadrillion suns. Like water flowing down a valley, all these galaxies are sliding toward the great attractor. On the outskirts, our own Milky Way remains locked in this giant flow.
